answer.evidence: The whole sign is a face-on vertical panel. The top header (rows 1-5) is a front-facing gray block with a white label oval. Width goes 8, 14, 16, then 14, so it is a flat-bottomed hat on a 14-wide body, not an ellipse. There is no front-edge line or eave shadow, only a dark outline at row 6. The green panel (rows 7-26) and the base cap (rows 27-31) are also vertical faces with no horizontal surface visible, so nothing reads as a top and the object is front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical green capsule sign with a lighter panel and a cross/text glyph. It has about 5 lightness steps across the green body, panel and trim, and shows a highlight edge and a darker side shade. Its dark edge pixels are tinted dark teal-green, not neutral (0% near-neutral, matching all three references), so the outline is a dark material tone. Near-flat coverage is 0%, against 9% for bus-shelter-a. It has 10 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and just under kiosk-a (12), but below vending-a (20). That puts it slightly below the richest reference, which is acceptable for a thin single-tile sign. The panel and glyph break up the surface, so there are no flat fills. A careful artist would accept it next to these shipped references without it looking like a flat sticker.
